argument_summary: The certification position should be read narrowly. The admissible record supports that aggregate release readiness is met and rehearsal showed no severity-one incidents, and it also supports using monitored, reversible deployment as part of risk management. The same record also establishes that the mortgage servicing assistant hardship forbearance segment remains below target and remains exposed in the initial 5% rollout, and that the draft risk acceptance is neither approved nor responsive to that exposure. On that record, the supportable defense is not that rollout controls cure the issue. It is that certification can proceed only as caveated compliance if launch is conditioned on explicit model-card disclosure of the named limitation for the affected use case before release, with monitoring and rollback operating as supplementary controls rather than policy substitutes.
claims_about_business_cost: No business-cost argument is needed to support the policy analysis, and no request here depends on launch-velocity considerations.
claims_about_policy: The policy text is the controlling constraint. It says rollout controls and post-launch monitoring mitigate a material model-card weakness only if the affected use case is excluded or there is reviewed risk acceptance explaining why exposure is acceptable. The admissible evidence shows neither predicate is satisfied here. Separately, the release policy requires material limitations for named launch use cases to be disclosed unless resolved or covered by approved risk acceptance before launch. That makes disclosure the only supportable path in the present record. The actor therefore narrows its claim: this is not present clean compliance on rollout controls alone; it is, at most, certification conditioned on disclosure being in place before launch.
concessions: The affected mortgage servicing assistant segment remains exposed in the initial rollout.
The unapproved risk acceptance draft does not provide valid policy cover for that exposure.
Aggregate readiness and clean rehearsal results do not override the disclosure requirement.
The current record does not prove that the required model-card disclosure has already been completed before launch.
